name: xxd
one_line: make a hex dump of a file, or turn a hex dump back into a file
plain: `xxd` shows the raw bytes of a file as hexadecimal numbers next to their text. It also works in reverse: give it hex and it rebuilds the bytes.
When a file will not open, hides data at its end, or you just need to see what is really in it, a hex dump is the ground truth: names and extensions can lie, bytes cannot.
when: Check a file's first bytes (its magic number) or the end of it for appended data.
Read hex from a challenge, a packet or a log and turn it back into bytes or text.
Edit one byte of a file: dump, change the hex, reverse.

mistakes: Forgetting -p when you reverse plain hex: without it xxd -r expects the full dump layout.
Hex digits are pairs: an odd number of digits is a typo (or a lost zero).
Reading little-endian numbers backwards: the bytes ef be ad de are the number 0xdeadbeef on x86.
Editing a file in place without keeping a copy.
